chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from some of our companions, from Amr ibn Ilyas, who said:

I performed Hajj with my father while I was a 'sarur' (one who has not yet performed the obligatory Hajj), and I said: 'I would like to make my Hajj on behalf of my mother, for she has died.' He said: 'Let me ask Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) for you.' Ilyas said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was listening: 'I am your ransom, this son of mine is a sarur, and his mother has died, and he wishes to make his Hajj on her behalf. Is that permissible for him?' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It is written for him and for her, and the reward of the act of piety is written for him, because in the report it is not established that the son was obligated to perform Hajj, but rather it implied that he was a sarur. And it is not impossible that what was obligatory upon him was the Hajj of Islam, and he merely volunteered to perform Hajj and intended by that Hajj on behalf of his mother, so it suffices for both of them. However, his state is not devoid of two matters: either he intended by it the Hajj on behalf of his mother regarding what was obligatory upon her, then it does not suffice for her and the Hajj remains obligatory upon him from his own wealth, as we have mentioned in the hadith of Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him). Or if he intends the Hajj for himself and for her together, then it suffices for him and the mother is entitled to the reward, even if the obligation of the Hajj of Islam is not lifted from her. And that which indicates this is...'

key_terms.ثَوَابُ أَجرِ البِرّ: The reward of the act of piety
key_terms.صَرُورَةٌ: A person who has not yet performed the obligatory Hajj

ai.seo_question: Can a son who hasn't performed his own obligatory Hajj perform Hajj on behalf of his deceased mother?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* clarifies the jurisprudential nuance of a 'sarur' (one who has not yet performed obligatory Hajj) performing Hajj on behalf of a deceased parent, emphasizing that the validity depends on the specific intention (*niyyah*). Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between dedicating the act solely to the mother’s debt—requiring the son to perform his own obligatory Hajj later—or combining both intentions, which satisfies the son’s duty while granting the mother reward. This ruling underscores the Shia principle that voluntary acts can accrue reward for the deceased even if the performer’s own obligatory duty remains pending, provided the intention is correctly specified.
